blinding_guess.why: B ships a test suite that maps one test to each requirement (including a stdlib-only AST test) and has injectable now/out/err, which suggests a spec-driven process; A is more polished but untested.

notes: Both sides implement every subcommand, overlap detection (log and report), HH:MM:SS output (including >24h) and refusal to start while a session is active; probes exercised these through TIME_TRACKER_FILE in temp dirs. A passed all 16 probes; B failed corrupt-JSON handling and blank-project rejection. A's only flaw found is a naive/aware datetime crash on foreign data. B's 7 unit tests pass when run with PYTHONPATH=B; A has no tests. Local interpreter is Python 3.9, so the P01 stdlib probe uses an explicit allowlist.
